inclusion.I1: English language empirical studies with original data
inclusion.I2: Functional MRI scan conducted while human participants performed a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task
inclusion.I3: Sample- humans of any age that were either healthy participants, substance users, as well as groups with other neuropsychiatric conditions

exclusion.E1: Studies using only PET or other non-fMRI neuroimaging methods

inclusion.I4: Functional MRI (fMRI) scan conducted while human participants performed a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task
inclusion.I5: At least one contrast comparing two decision-making conditions, or a decision-making task against an active CONTROL TASK. The admitted forms are- for risky-DM "risky > safe", "high-risk > low-risk", "risk > certainty", "riskier > surer", or "experimental task (risk) > control task"; for ambiguous-DM "high uncertainty > low uncertainty", "ambiguity > ignorance", "ambiguous > non-ambiguous", or "ambiguous task > control task"; for perceptual-DM "hard > easy", "low coherence > high coherence", or "perceptual task > control task". Both within-task and between-task comparisons qualify.
inclusion.I6: Whole-brain evidence- The target analysis must be a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map
inclusion.I7: Any participant group qualifies- healthy participants, substance users, and participants with other neuropsychiatric conditions (internet addiction, gambling disorder, internet gaming disorder, obesity, depressive, anxiety or conduct disorders, antisocial personality disorder, schizophrenia). All age groups from roughly 10 to 69 years qualify. Do not exclude a study because of who its participants were.
inclusion.I8: It is acceptable for qualifying whole-brain results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials, as long as they are clearly described in the text.

exclusion.E3: Studies whose only decision-making contrasts are against an implicit baseline, rest or fixation (e.g. "50% probability condition > implicit baseline", "task > rest"). This benchmark admits only condition-versus-condition and task-versus-control-task contrasts.
exclusion.E4: Positron emission tomography (PET) studies. The source meta-analysis excluded PET deliberately, to remove heterogeneity across imaging modalities.
exclusion.E5: Studies whose decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous or perceptual DM- for example delay discounting or intertemporal choice, moral or social decision-making, reward receipt or consumption without an uncertainty manipulation, and effort-based choice.
exclusion.E6: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no whole-brain results.
exclusion.E7: Studies that report only seed-based connectivity, effective connectivity (e.g., PPI, DCM), or resting-state analyses (e.g., ICA, PLE, Hurst exponents) without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map.
exclusion.E8: Studies that report ONLY between-group contrasts or interactions (e.g. substance users vs non-users, patient vs control) with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect. Note this is about the contrast, not the sample- a within-group contrast in a patient or substance-using sample qualifies.
exclusion.E9: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original fMRI data.

inclusion.GLOBAL_I2: Whole-brain evidence- Must be a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map
inclusion.GLOBAL_I3: If an analysis label is generic/truncated (e.g., analysis_0), use table caption, neighboring contrasts, and study_fulltext to infer eligibility; do not fail only because the label text is sparse.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I4: Resolve subtype overlaps by primary uncertainty source- sensory evidence uncertainty -> perceptual_dm; uncertainty/ambiguity in contingencies or information -> ambiguous_dm; explicit known-risk vs safe/certain choice -> risky_dm.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I5: Study-level subtype mutual exclusivity is required- for each study/PMID, assign exactly one subtype among ambiguous_dm, perceptual_dm, and risky_dm.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I6: Once a study-level subtype is chosen, all included analyses from that study must follow that same subtype; do not split analyses from one study across multiple subtypes.

exclusion.GLOBAL_E2: Seed-based connectivity, effective connectivity (e.g., PPI, DCM), or resting-state analyses (e.g., ICA, PLE, Hurst exponents)

inclusion.COMMON_DM_I1: contrasts related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making
inclusion.COMMON_DM_I2: all populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, drug users, patients with substance use disorders, or other neuropsychiatric conditions)

inclusion.AMBIGUOUS_DM_I1: assign this annotation only if ambiguous_dm is the single study-level subtype for that PMID.
inclusion.AMBIGUOUS_DM_I2: contrasts where uncertainty/ambiguity is central to the decision (e.g., “ambiguous > certain”, “high uncertainty > low uncertainty”, “ambiguity > risk”, uncertainty-driven information sampling/decision contrasts).
inclusion.AMBIGUOUS_DM_I3: include uncertainty-based choice contrasts even when labels are generic (analysis_0/analysis_1) if study/table context shows they are uncertainty decision maps.
inclusion.AMBIGUOUS_DM_I4: all populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, drug users, patients with substance use disorders, or other neuropsychiatric conditions)

exclusion.AMBIGUOUS_DM_E1: exclude sensory-perceptual difficulty contrasts (e.g., low coherence > high coherence, noisy > clear, hard > easy perceptual discrimination); those belong in perceptual_dm.
exclusion.AMBIGUOUS_DM_E2: exclude purely outcome/feedback contrasts unless the contrast directly indexes uncertainty during the decision phase.

inclusion.PERCEPTUAL_DM_I1: assign this annotation only if perceptual_dm is the single study-level subtype for that PMID.
inclusion.PERCEPTUAL_DM_I2: contrasts where decisions are based on sensory/perceptual evidence (e.g., coherence/noise/category discrimination, hard > easy perceptual judgments, perceptual task > control).
inclusion.PERCEPTUAL_DM_I3: include low-coherence/noisy > high-coherence/clear contrasts as perceptual_dm, not ambiguous_dm.
inclusion.PERCEPTUAL_DM_I4: all populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, drug users, patients with substance use disorders, or other neuropsychiatric conditions)

exclusion.PERCEPTUAL_DM_E1: exclude economic/probability uncertainty, reward prediction, or gambling ambiguity/risk contrasts even if stimuli are visual.

inclusion.RISKY_DM_I1: assign this annotation only if risky_dm is the single study-level subtype for that PMID.
inclusion.RISKY_DM_I2: contrasts with explicit known-risk manipulation focused on risky vs safe/certain choice (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty, riskier > surer, risk task > control).
inclusion.RISKY_DM_I3: all populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, drug users, patients with substance use disorders, or other neuropsychiatric conditions)

exclusion.RISKY_DM_E1: exclude ambiguity-dominant contrasts (e.g., ambiguity > risk, mixed risk-vs-ambiguity contrasts where ambiguity is the target); route these to ambiguous_dm.
exclusion.RISKY_DM_E2: exclude generic uncertainty/prediction contrasts without a clear risky-vs-safe decision manipulation.

inclusion.NON_USING_RISKY_I1: only apply when the study-level subtype for that PMID is risky_dm.
inclusion.NON_USING_RISKY_I2: same risky_dm contrast rules: explicit known-risk vs safe/certain choice contrasts; exclude ambiguity-dominant or generic uncertainty-only contrasts.
inclusion.NON_USING_RISKY_I3: non-substance using populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, or other neuropsychiatric conditions) compared to substance using populations (e.g., drug users, patients with substance use disorders)

inclusion.USING_RISKY_I1: only apply when the study-level subtype for that PMID is risky_dm.
inclusion.USING_RISKY_I2: same risky_dm contrast rules: explicit known-risk vs safe/certain choice contrasts; exclude ambiguity-dominant or generic uncertainty-only contrasts.
inclusion.USING_RISKY_I3: substance using populations (e.g., drug users, patients with substance use disorders) compared to non-substance using populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, or other neuropsychiatric conditions)
